<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Transformers v5 may drop `add_bos_token` and `add_eos_token` settings when
loading a tokenizer backed by `tokenizer.json`. It assumes that the serialized
tokenizer post-processor already handles BOS/EOS insertion, but that is not true
for every tokenizer configuration.

SGLang already compensates for this behavior in `get_tokenizer()` by reading
`tokenizer_config.json`, restoring the supported flags, and rebuilding the
tokenizer post-processor.

SGLang has two related loading entry points:

- `get_tokenizer()` returns a tokenizer directly and is typically used by
  text-only loading paths.
- `get_processor()` returns a multimodal processor that owns a tokenizer in
  addition to image, audio, or other preprocessing components.

Both entry points ultimately tokenize the text portion of a request, so their
tokenizer compatibility behavior should be consistent. Before this change,
only the direct `get_tokenizer()` path applied the Transformers-v5 BOS/EOS
repair. The tokenizer embedded in a processor bypassed it.

This does not affect every model. The compatibility helper is limited to
tokenizer classes that supported these flags before Transformers v5, currently
including Llama, Code Llama, Gemma, and Cohere tokenizers. It is a no-op for
other tokenizer classes and for configurations whose values are already
correct.

Multimodal models commonly load the same tokenizer through `get_processor()`.
That path extracts the processor-owned tokenizer and applies several post-load
fixes, but it does not apply the existing BOS/EOS compatibility repair. The same
checkpoint can therefore tokenize a prompt differently depending on which
loading entry point is used. For affected Gemma tokenizers, the processor path
can omit the expected BOS token.

This change does not alter Transformers itself or introduce a new compatibility
policy. It applies SGLang's existing policy consistently to the tokenizer owned
by a processor.

## Modifications

- Apply the existing `_fix_v5_add_bos_eos_token()` helper to the final tokenizer
  selected by `get_processor()`.
- Keep the compatibility policy in one place rather than duplicating it in the
  processor loader.
- Add a CPU-only regression test that loads a local Gemma tokenizer
  configuration through the processor path and verifies that `add_bos_token`
  is restored and the tokenizer post-processor is rebuilt.

The helper already limits restoration to tokenizer classes that supported
these flags before Transformers v5. Unsupported tokenizer classes and
tokenizers with correct settings remain unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

This changes tokenizer initialization rather than model execution. The added
CPU regression test verifies the affected tokenization state without model
weights or accelerator hardware.

- Focused unit test: pending GitHub CI.
- Python syntax check: passed.
- `black --check`: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The compatibility repair runs once while loading a processor
and does not affect the inference hot path.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No documentation change is needed for this loader consistency fix.
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Focused correctness coverage is pending CI; performance is unaffected.
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

@@ -6,8 +6,10 @@
 
 import inspect
 import io
+import json
 import tempfile
 import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
 from types import SimpleNamespace
 from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch
 
@@ -47,6 +49,61 @@
 
 
 class TestGetProcessor(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_applies_v5_bos_eos_fix_to_processor_tokenizer(self):
+        class ProcessorTokenizer:
+            chat_template = "template"
+
+            def __init__(self):
+                self._add_bos_token = False
+                self._add_eos_token = False
+                self.update_post_processor_calls = 0
+
+            @property
+            def add_bos_token(self):
+                return self._add_bos_token
+
+            @property
+            def add_eos_token(self):
+                return self._add_eos_token
+
+            def update_post_processor(self):
+                self.update_post_processor_calls += 1
+
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as model_path:
+            Path(model_path, "tokenizer_config.json").write_text(
+                json.dumps(
+                    {
+                        "tokenizer_class": "GemmaTokenizer",
+                        "add_bos_token": True,
+                        "add_eos_token": False,
+                    }
+                )
+            )
+            config = SimpleNamespace(model_type="test_vlm", auto_map={})
+            tokenizer = ProcessorTokenizer()
+            loaded_processor = SimpleNamespace(tokenizer=tokenizer)
+            auto_config = MagicMock()
+            auto_config.from_pretrained.return_value = config
+            auto_processor = MagicMock()
+            auto_processor.from_pretrained.return_value = loaded_processor
+
+            with patch.multiple(
+                processor_utils,
+                AutoConfig=auto_config,
+                AutoProcessor=auto_processor,
+                _install_tokenizer_warnings_filter=MagicMock(),
+                patch_mistral_common_tokenizer=MagicMock(),
+                _fix_special_tokens_pattern=MagicMock(),
+                _fix_added_tokens_encoding=MagicMock(),
+                attach_additional_stop_token_ids=MagicMock(),
+            ):
+                processor = processor_utils.get_processor(model_path)
+
+        self.assertIs(processor, loaded_processor)
+        self.assertTrue(tokenizer.add_bos_token)
+        self.assertFalse(tokenizer.add_eos_token)
+        self.assertEqual(tokenizer.update_post_processor_calls, 1)
+
     def test_does_not_forward_backend_to_auto_processor(self):
         config = SimpleNamespace(model_type="test_vlm", auto_map={})
         loaded_processor = MagicMock()
